title: 2026届高三英语听力仿真训练（19）｜健康心理
note: 原创仿真训练，按 2026 高考听力题型编写（第一节、第二节均播放两遍）。

sections.name: 第一节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话。每段对话后有一个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听完每段对话后，你都有10秒钟的时间来回答有关小题和阅读下一小题。每段对话读两遍。

materials.label: 第1段材料
materials.transcript:
W: I've been going to bed at one in the morning and still feel tired.
M: Do you use your phone in bed?
W: Only for a while. Why?
M: The light keeps your brain awake. Put the phone outside the bedroom for a week.

questions.text: What does the man tell the woman to do?

options.B: Take a short sleep in the day.
options.C: Keep her phone out of the bedroom.

materials.label: 第2段材料
materials.transcript:
M: You look tired. What time did you go to bed?
W: Half past twelve. My alarm went off at half past six.
M: That's only six hours. You need eight.
W: I know. I'll try to be in bed by ten thirty tonight.

questions.text: How long did the woman sleep?

materials.label: 第3段材料
materials.transcript:
W: I've started drinking energy drinks before morning classes.
M: How many a day?
W: Two or three. They help me stay awake.
M: They do, for an hour. Then you crash and you can't sleep at night. I'd cut them out.

questions.text: What does the man think of energy drinks?

options.A: They are a good choice for students.
options.B: They cause more problems than they solve.
options.C: They should be sold at school.

materials.label: 第4段材料
materials.transcript:
W: I can't sleep before the maths test. My hands shake when I open the paper.
M: Have you talked to Ms. Yang? She is the school counselor.
W: I thought only failing students went to her.
M: Not at all. Half my class has seen her this term.

questions.text: What does the man advise the woman to do?

materials.label: 第5段材料
materials.transcript:
M: The pool opens at two and closes at seven. The student session is the last two hours.
W: So it starts at five? I finish class at half past four.
M: Right. And the bus takes twenty minutes, so you'd be there by ten to five.
W: Good. I'll bring my card.

questions.text: When does the student session start?

sections.name: 第二节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话或独白。每段对话或独白后有几个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听每段对话或独白前，你将有时间阅读各个小题，每小题5秒钟；听完后，各小题将给出5秒钟的作答时间。每段对话或独白读两遍。

materials.label: 第6段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Good morning, this is the school health centre.
M: Hello. I've had a headache for three days, and I can't sleep.
W: Any other symptoms? A cough, or a sore throat?
M: No cough. But I feel dizzy when I stand up quickly.
W: Are you free at four this afternoon? Dr. Lin has a free slot then.
M: I have a physics class until four thirty.
W: Then come at nine tomorrow morning. Please don't eat breakfast before the blood test.
M: All right. Should I bring anything?
W: Your student card and this form. Drink some water before you come.
M: Will the doctor ask about my screen time?
W: Probably. Bring a note of the hours you sleep, and try to keep the same bedtime this week.

questions.text: When will the man see the doctor?
What should the man do before the test?

materials.label: 第7段材料
materials.transcript:
M: You look pale. Are you all right?
W: I've been studying until one every night. The exams start on Monday.
M: That won't help. Your brain needs sleep to remember things.
W: I know, but there is too much to review. And my phone keeps me awake. I answer messages at midnight.
M: Leave it in the kitchen after ten. You will not miss anything important.
W: Maybe. What else?
M: Try studying in the morning instead. I get up at six and work for two hours before school. Then I stop at ten at night.
W: Doesn't that feel strange at first?
M: For a week. Then your body gets used to it. I also walk for twenty minutes after dinner, which clears my head.
W: I might try the morning plan. But six o'clock is very early.
M: Start with twenty minutes at seven, then build up.

questions.text: What does the man think of the woman's study plan?

options.A: It will help her remember more.
options.B: It will do her more harm than good.
options.C: It is the only way to pass the exam.

questions.text: What does the man suggest the woman do?
What does the man do after dinner?

materials.label: 第8段材料
materials.transcript:
W: You've had nothing but noodles and cola for two days.
M: I was busy. And I'm not hungry in the morning. I drink cola when I study.
W: That's sugar and caffeine. Replace one bottle a day with water.
M: All right. But I'm still not hungry at seven in the morning.
W: That's the problem. Skipping breakfast makes you eat more at night.
M: What should I have, then?
W: An egg, some milk and a fruit. It takes five minutes. And take the stairs instead of the lift.
M: The stairs? We live on the eighth floor.
W: Then get off the lift two floors early. Start small, and add more each week.
M: Two floors still feels like a lot.
W: Do you eat vegetables at school?
M: Only when my friends do.
W: Then take the small dish. In a month you won't notice the stairs at all.

questions.text: What has the man been eating?
What does the woman say about skipping breakfast?

options.B: It saves a lot of time.
options.C: It makes you eat more later.

questions.text: What does the woman suggest about exercise?

options.A: Using the stairs a little every day.
options.B: Joining a gym near the school.

materials.label: 第9段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Ms. Yang, more students come to you before exams than at any other time. Why?
W: They think they are the only ones who feel nervous. When they talk, they find out everyone does.
M: What do you tell them first?
W: To sleep. A tired brain makes small problems look huge. Eight hours is part of the work, not a luxury.
M: What about the students who study all night?
W: They often do worse. They can repeat facts but cannot use them. Exams ask you to think.
M: Any practical advice?
W: Study in blocks of forty minutes, then stand up and move for five. And write down tomorrow's three main tasks before you sleep.
M: Anything parents should stop doing?
W: Comparing their child with a cousin or a neighbour. That kind of talk stays for years.

questions.text: Why do students feel nervous before exams?

options.B: They think others are not nervous.

questions.text: What does Ms. Yang say about students who study all night?

options.B: They need coffee to stay awake.

questions.text: What does Ms. Yang suggest doing after forty minutes of study?
What does Ms. Yang say parents should avoid?

materials.label: 第10段材料
materials.transcript: Three weeks ago I decided to change three things for a month: sleep, food and movement. I set my alarm for ten in the evening, not to wake up, but to remind me to put my phone down. On the fourth night I fell asleep before eleven. For food, I added a fruit to breakfast and stopped buying sweet drinks. That was harder than I expected, because my friends buy them every day. For movement, I walked to school twice a week instead of taking the bus. The walk takes twenty-five minutes; the bus takes fifteen. So I lost ten minutes each time and gained a clear head. My marks did not jump, but I stopped falling asleep in the third class. In a month, three small changes were enough. That, for me, is a real win.

questions.text: What was the ten o'clock alarm for?

options.B: To make the speaker put down his phone.
options.C: To remind the speaker to do homework.

questions.text: Which change was the hardest for the speaker?
How much longer does the walk take than the bus?
